classification.difficultyReason: The hardest parts require interpreting an integer parameter as an entire discrete family of translated curves; other parts connect factored equations to unions of graphs.

content.prompt: Sketch the following sets of points in the Euclidean plane:

answer.short: The filled square $[1,2]\times[1,2]$, including its boundary.
answer.worked: The conditions are $1\le x\le2$ and $1\le y\le2$. Draw the square with vertices $(1,1)$, $(2,1)$, $(2,2)$ and $(1,2)$, and shade its interior. All four sides are included.

spec.description: Closed square in the first quadrant; light blue fill represents set membership.

answer.short: The filled rectangle $[0,1]\times[1,2]$, including its boundary.
answer.worked: The conditions are $0\le x\le1$ and $1\le y\le2$. Draw the square with vertices $(0,1)$, $(1,1)$, $(1,2)$ and $(0,2)$, and shade its interior. All four sides are included.

spec.description: Closed square adjoining the positive y-axis; fill represents set membership.

answer.short: The horizontal segment from $(-1,1)$ to $(1,1)$, including both endpoints.
answer.worked: Every point has $y=1$, while $-1\le x\le1$. Draw the horizontal segment joining $(-1,1)$ and $(1,1)$ with closed endpoints.

spec.description: Horizontal segment with two closed endpoints.

answer.short: The vertical segment from $(1,0)$ to $(1,1)$, including both endpoints.
answer.worked: Every point has $x=1$, while $0\le y\le1$. Draw the vertical segment joining $(1,0)$ and $(1,1)$ with closed endpoints.

spec.description: Vertical segment with lower closed endpoint on the x-axis.

answer.worked: Draw the solid boundary $y=x$. Shade above the line, since those points satisfy $y\ge x$. The boundary is included.

spec.description: Bounded viewing window showing the unbounded half-plane above a solid diagonal.
spec.mathematics: y≥x; the viewing-window edges are not boundaries.

answer.short: The half-plane to the right of $x=1$, excluding the boundary.
answer.worked: Draw the dashed boundary $x=1$. Shade to its right. The strict inequality excludes points on the boundary.

spec.description: Half-plane right of a dashed vertical boundary; fill represents membership.
spec.mathematics: x>1; the viewing-window edges are not boundaries.

answer.short:
$y=x+n$ for every $n\in\mathbb Z$.

Parallel lines of gradient 1 with integer $y$-intercepts.
answer.worked: The second coordinate gives $y=x+n$. For each integer $n$, draw the entire line of gradient 1 with $y$-intercept $n$. These include $y=x$, $y=x\pm1$, $y=x\pm2$, and continue for all integer values of $n$.

spec.description: Representative window of the infinite family of parallel lines.
spec.mathematics: y=x+n for all integers n; all lines intersecting the open viewing window are shown.

answer.short:
$y=x^2+n$ for every $n\in\mathbb Z$.

Upward parabolas with vertices $(0,n)$ at every integer height.
answer.worked: The second coordinate gives $y=x^2+n$. Draw $y=x^2$ and its vertical translates by every integer amount. Each parabola has vertex $(0,n)$ and axis of symmetry the $y$-axis.

spec.description: Representative window of upward parabolas translated by integer amounts.
spec.mathematics: y=x²+n for all integers n; the family continues beyond the window.

answer.worked: A product is zero when at least one factor is zero. Thus $y-x=0$ or $y+x=0$, giving $y=x$ or $y=-x$. Draw both entire lines through the origin.

spec.description: Two diagonal lines crossing at the origin.

answer.worked: A product is zero when at least one factor is zero. Thus $y-x^2=0$ or $y+x^2=0$, giving $y=x^2$ or $y=-x^2$. Draw both parabolas with vertex $(0,0)$, one opening upward and the other downward.

spec.description: Upward and downward parabolas sharing the origin as vertex.
